newsitem.title: USA: SmithKline's Coreg cleared for heart failure.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline's Coreg cleared for heart failure.

text.p: SmithKline Beecham Plc said Thursday that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has cleared Coreg (carvedilol) for the treatment of congestive heart failure.
Coreg, which was jointly developed by SmithKline and Boehringer Mannheim GmbH, combines non-selective beta-blocking and vasodilating properties.
According to SmithKline, the drug represents a new approach to the treatment of heart failure and is the first agent of its type to be cleared in the U.S. for the heart-failure indication.
Coreg is now cleared for the treatment of heart failure in 15 countries.
In the U.S. and other countries, Coreg is also approved for the treatment of hypertension. However, the dosing regimen and precautions for use for hypertension differ from those for heart failure.
The company said that Coreg is indicated for the treatment of patients with mild or moderate heart failure, who represent the majority of heart-failure patients.
